pr_title: Bluetooth: ISO: Add seq_num and ts to bt_iso_chan_send
pr_body:
Add two new parameters to bt_iso_chan_send:
sn: The packet sequence number which shall be incremeted per SDU interval.
ts: An optional timestamp value used to synchronize SDUs.

Signed-off-by: Emil Gydesen <emil.gydesen@nordicsemi.no>

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/43859
pr_comments: Added DNM as I am awaiting response on https://www.bluetooth.org/errata/errata_view.cfm?errata_id=18552 to see if this is truly the right way of doing it, or if the spec is unclear or unintentionally creating a bad requirement from the host.

Removing DNM as we have a workaround for the erratum. 

Updated the shell to calculate the next sequence number instead of incrementing it. 

Updated the sequence number to use uint32_t instead of uint16_t.
Added a new commit to rename `sn` to `seq_num` as per request from @cvinayak: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45436#discussion_r887561157

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: ISO: Add sequence number and timestamp to bt_iso_chan_send
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently the stack sets the sequence number and does not provide at timestamp when sending SDUs to the controller. This make the `bt_iso_chan_send` much less flexible, and may even be too unflexible in some cases. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Append a sequence number and time stamp parameter to the function such that 
```c
int bt_iso_chan_send(struct bt_iso_chan *chan, struct net_buf *buf);
```
becomes
```c
int bt_iso_chan_send(struct bt_iso_chan *chan, struct net_buf *buf, uint16_t sn, uint32_t ts);
```
The timestamp, as per the core spec, shall be an optional parameter. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
This change may require a chan in the `bt_audio_chan_send` as well.

review_comments: Timing is changed with a factor of ten here - is that intentional?
Timing was changed to match the SDU interval, which is intentional as we want to use this callback to increment the SN per SDU interval
And here there is factor of ten change in the other direction (10 ms -> 100 ms)
Hmm, I actually don't remember, nor do I see any reason, to change from 10ms to 100ms. Will change back to 10ms.

Is it a good thing to have this "shall" here?
This is the struct, is this the right place to mandate behavior?  And if we do, should it say who is responsible to increment it?
Propose to end sentence after sequence number".
I think it's fine to keep it in this (internal) struct, as that will serve as a comment for developers if they attempt to change how the `seq_num` is handled
It is, but the ISO API is still considered experimental, so we can do changes like this without worrying too much :)
ok, I've only checked CONFIG_BT_ISO_UNICAST and BT_ISO_BROADCAST and those aren't market as experimental :)

`CONFIG_BT_ISO_UNICAST` and `BT_ISO_BROADCAST` are "hidden" Kconfigs, enabled by `BT_ISO_PERIPHERAL`, `BT_ISO_CENTRAL`, `BT_ISO_BROADCASTER` and `BT_ISO_SYNC_RECEIVER` which all are marked as Experimental :) But I see where the confusion stems from
